title: The Bank of England's fees regime for financial market infrastructure supervision 2026/27
summary: The Bank of England has published a consultation paper on its proposed supervisory fees for financial market infrastructure (FMI) for the 2026/27 fee year, covering fee rates and an extension to the phased recovery period for UK CCP rulebook costs. The consultation deadline is 18 May 2026 and is relevant to all FMIs that currently pay or expect to pay supervision fees to the Bank.
key_points: Bank of England proposing 2026/27 FMI supervisory fee rates to meet funding requirement for FMI supervision and supporting policy activity
Extension to phased recovery period for UK CCP rulebook costs is included in proposals
Responses to consultation requested by 18 May 2026
FSMA 2023 gave the Bank rulemaking powers following UK's exit from EU; CCP rulebook work nearing completion, CSD rulebook being scoped
Digital Securities Sandbox (DSS) supervision fees expected to begin in 2026/27 fee year
Overall FMI directorate costs reduced over past year reflecting Bank-wide focus on efficiencies
Bank's secondary innovation objective includes supervisory approach for onboarding new FMIs with mobilization phase
